raw: {"need": "Competence", "secondary": {"name": "Belonging"}, "read": "Before they have done a single thing, they are already calculating whether they can actually succeed here. Showing up on day one without knowing the rules is not just disorienting, it is a status threat disguised as a logistical problem. If the expectations land as a long list of ways to fail, their nervous system will treat the job as a test they are already behind on.", "pull": {"collapse": "Enforcer", "instinct": "Front-load every policy, standard, and consequence on day one so nothing is ambiguous, which turns the first day into an audit they cannot possibly pass and teaches them the job is about surviving you rather than building something."}, "mentorMove": "Name one or two expectations that actually matter this week, explain why they matter to the work and to the team, and make clear you are the person they come to when they are unsure, not the person they hide from when they slip up.", "holdFirm": ["The core standards apply from day one, not after some grace period.", "Asking for help and flagging confusion early is a professional expectation, not optional."], "stayFlexible": ["Which expectations you introduce in week one versus week two or three.", "Whether you deliver them in a meeting, a short written summary, or a walk-around where things come up naturally."], "forceLevel": {"level": 1, "label": "Empathy"}, "script": [{"phase": "Connection", "words": "Starting somewhere new is a lot, even when you are excited about it. The first week your brain is doing a lot of work just figuring out where things are and how things move, so I want to make this landing as clean as possible for you."}, {"phase": "Curiosity", "words": "Before I tell you anything, what feels most uncertain right now? What would make Monday feel less like a guessing game?"}, {"phase": "Collaboration", "words": "Here is what I am going to do. I will give you the two or three things that matter most this week, so you know where to put your attention. Everything else we will build in as you get your footing. And when something is unclear, I want to hear it from you directly before it becomes a problem, because that is how good work actually happens."}, {"phase": "Commitment", "words": "I am holding you to a real standard here, not a probationary one, because I would not have hired you if I did not think you could meet it. The standard is the same on day one as it is on day ninety. What changes is how much of the context you have to work with, and that part I am going to make sure you get."}], "longGame": "The goal is that by the end of the first month they understand the expectations well enough to explain them to the next new hire. That kind of ownership does not come from a policy handout on day one; it comes from a manager who treated the standards as something worth understanding, not just enforcing."}
situation: A new hire starts Monday and I want to set clear expectations without overwhelming them.
